subject: Token & throughput alignment for MAP — batching, caching, and close timeline
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@medicorehealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@medicorehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 08:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: cost sensitivity for MAP

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile. As we pull together the mutual action plan (MAP) to present to procurement, finance needs a short, defensible breakdown of token economics and the assumptions you used for batching and caching. Specifically: tokens per response assumptions, expected cache hit rates for patient Q&A flows, and how batching will impact peak concurrency during our pilot (50k monthly sessions projected).

Can you send a concise calc + a recommended gating timeline we can include in the MAP (pilot -> expand)? Procurement prefers a single-slide summary and an appendix spreadsheet.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of Platform Integrations, Medicore Health
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@medicorehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: cost sensitivity for MAP

Elena — thanks for the note. High level response below; attaching a spreadsheet with the worked numbers (token-econ-model-v2.xlsx).

TL;DR: For the pilot profile you shared (short Q&A, median response ~120 tokens, 95th pct < 400 tokens) our baseline assumes: 120 tokens/response, 2.0 requests/session, batching target of 16 for server-side throughput, and a conservative cache hit of 28% on prefix/FAQ matches. That yields ~tokens/dollar consistent with our hosted pricing tier; the attachment shows sensitivity at +/-20% for each lever.

Assumptions to call out in the MAP slide:
- Response token distribution: median 120, mean ~150 (we model a heavy tail).
- Batching: ops target to group small requests into micro-batches of 8–16 while preserving p50 latency under 220ms.
- Caching: prefix and FAQ caching modeled separately; we used a 28% overall hit rate for user intent repeats and 10% for exact-match prefixes.
- Fallbacks: canary to smaller quantized model (8-bit) if latency SLOs breach at peak.

Proposed MAP gating timeline (short):
- Week 0: Pilot kickoff, instrumentation and traffic capture (2 wks)
- Week 2–4: Run pilot at real traffic, tune batching thresholds and caching TTLs
- Week 4: Cost sanity check and unit-econ signoff (finance + procurement)
- Week 6: Expand to 2x traffic if unit economics meet target

Marissa — can you add the ops notes on batching guardrails and the typical tradeoffs we should call out in the MAP slide?

David
David Kim
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@medicorehealth.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: cost sensitivity for MAP

Elena — quick ops-level detail to include in the MAP appendix so your engineering and SRE teams can validate: 

1) Batching mechanics and impact:
- For short Q&A sessions we recommend an adaptive batching window: 8–16 tokens-per-request grouping for p50/well-behaved traffic, with an upper bound of 32 to protect SLOs during spikes.
- Batching improves tokens/$ primarily by increasing throughput on GPU kernels (amortizes KV cache loads). We modeled a 15–30% tokens/$ improvement at median traffic when moving from no-batching -> batch size ~16.

2) Caching assumptions:
- Two-tier cache: (A) prefix/FAQ cache (cheap, high hit on repeated intent), (B) KV cache (session-level) to avoid recomputing prior context.
- We used a conservative prefix hit 25–30% (varies by UX); KV cache assumed 40% reuse within sessions for multi-turn dialogs.

3) Latency tradeoffs & SLOs:
- Adaptive batching has a tiny added p50 delay (5–30ms) but can reduce p95 costs significantly. If you need strict p95 < 300ms, we throttle batching and increase dedicated capacity.

4) Measurement hooks for the MAP:
- Instrument tokens/request, batch-size histogram, prefix-hit boolean, and end-to-end p50/p95. We can provide a sample Datadog dashboard.

I'll update the MAP-draft-20270812.pdf with these bullets and a short ops checklist. Quick Q: do you have a target unit-econ (tokens/$) threshold procurement expects for pilot approval?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Park <elena.park@medicorehealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 13:29:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: cost sensitivity for MAP

Thanks — this is helpful. Procurement gave us a soft threshold: they want pilot costs to be at or below $0.12 per active patient session (tokens and inference compute only). For a 2-request/session baseline that maps to roughly X tokens/dollar — we'll need your workbook to translate to tokens/$ using Redwood's hosted tier assumptions.

Also: two compliance asks we need in the MAP appendix — max retention for logs (30 days) and an audit summary for request-level tracing. Can you confirm those are standard?

Tom (cc'd) — our SRE will share a sampled traffic CSV tomorrow to help you model the distribution.

Elena
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@medicorehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: cost sensitivity for MAP

Great — attaching the two files (token-econ-model-v2.xlsx, MAP-draft-20270812.pdf). Quick notes after running the numbers against your $0.12/session target: 

- Using pilot median 120 tokens/response and 2 reqs/session, our baseline tokens/session = 240. With the modeled batch (16) and cache hit 28%, effective billable tokens/session drops to ~175, which maps to an estimated cost of $0.10/session on Redwood hosted tier (spreadsheet shows the math).
- If your traffic skews longer (mean 220 tokens/response), cost rises close to $0.16/session — that's where caching and a small quantized fallback model help.

Compliance answers: 30-day retention for logs is supported by default in the Private/Dedicated options; hosted customers can configure retention down to 30 days via the Console. We also support request-level trace export to your SIEM; we'll include the audit summary in the MAP appendix.

Next steps and timeline I propose adding to the MAP slide: 
- Thu (this week): review spreadsheet and confirm target threshold; Marissa to finalize ops checklist.
- Mon (Week 2): ingest SRE traffic sample; run sensitivity sims.
- End Week 3: joint readout for procurement with slide + appendix.

I'll push updated files to the HubSpot deal record and the shared Drive folder (links above). Let me know if you want a brief walkthrough call after Tom's CSV comes in.

Best,
David
David Kim
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: token-econ-model-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), MAP-draft-20270812.pdf (one-slide MAP + appendix)
